## RCA and close record

**Landed.** Gerrit change 1977, merged as `cc3fba5cfb` on `origin/main` (`LLM-Review +1`,
`Verified +1`, no unresolved comments). Gerrit rebased on submit, so the merged commit is a
twin of the locally authored `b357096800`; `git diff` between the two restricted to this
ticket's two files is **empty**, and the suite passes on the merged tree.

### `caused_by`: `259c-0f29-e920-4fab`, class `plan_defect`

Established by the date test rather than by blaming the file I edited. The single-remedy
wording was introduced by `7cf80009d9` ("Block oversized ticket descriptions before review",
2026-08-10, `rebar-ticket: 259c-0f29-e920-4fab`) — the commit that made the description limit
**blocking** and wrote the remedy alongside it. Confirmed by `git log -S"usually by splitting"`,
which returns that commit and no other. The only earlier history at these lines is the
epic-5fd2 introduction of P4 as an **advisory** check with no blocking limit, which therefore
could not produce this coaching failure. The origin predates this bug's discovery (2026-08-20)
by ten days, so the file I edited is the genuine origin and not merely where the symptom
surfaced.

`plan_defect` ("the design/plan itself was wrong") rather than `regression`: the message never
worked correctly. It was single-remedy from the moment the check began blocking, so nothing
regressed. The 259c plan correctly specified rejecting oversized descriptions but assumed
over-length had a single cause, and wrote a single remedy to match. The defect is in that
design assumption.

**Mechanism note:** this build exposes `caused_by` as a **link relation**
(`rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`), not as a `--caused-by` flag on `transition` — checked
against both the global build and this worktree's build, and `rebar transition --help` lists
only `--class`, `--reason`, `--force`, `--ref`, `--output`. The edge is therefore recorded as a
link. The ticket carried no prior `caused_by` edge (its links were `discovered_from` 76b2,
`relates_to` fb8b, `supersedes` db74), so there is exactly one after this.

### Why "raise the cap" was foreclosed, recorded on the ticket

The 8,000-character limit exists to bound the **completion verifier's context window**. An
oversized description can exceed what the verifier is able to read, so the gate meant to confirm
the work degrades or fails — the limit protects a downstream consumer rather than expressing a
style preference. Raising it would reintroduce exactly the failure it was created to prevent, in
the gate whose job is to confirm completion. That is why raising the cap is foreclosed rather
than merely out of scope, and the diff moves no limit, no config key, and no default.

It is also the reason the new message coaches a **distinction** rather than a word count. If the
constraint were stylistic, "be shorter" would suffice. Because the constraint protects a reader
with a finite budget, the message has to say *which* material that reader needs — problem,
constraints, and each acceptance criterion with its evidence — and *which* material can move to
comments or a session log without loss. Coaching only brevity would fail the same gate from the
opposite direction, by producing a plan the reviewer cannot evaluate and the verifier cannot
check.

### Acceptance criteria

All six are met and ticked. AC4 is worth a note: it was satisfied by *creating* a distinction
rather than preserving one, because both P4 branches shared a single `suggested_fix` before this
change — the advisory too-many-criteria branch was also telling authors to cut characters. Each
branch now carries its own remedy.
